currentContext.business: The Company's main activity is manufacturing of coke and refined petroleum products, which accounts for 99.22% of turnover (BRSR Section A; Petroleum Products, NIC code 19201). Its portfolio spans transformer oils marketed under TRANSOL, bioTRANSOL and TRANSOL Synth; white and mineral oils and petroleum jellies under TECHNOL, SAVONOL and SAVOGEL; automotive and industrial lubricants under SAVSOL; and formulated specialty waxes, emulsions and cable compounds under SAVOFIL, SAVOFLOD and VITAGEL - sold to transformer manufacturers, power plant operators and electricity boards, to pharmaceutical, personal care, plastics and polymer customers, to automotive OEMs, and to retail customers through the B2C SAVSOL range. Operations comprise 4 plants and 5 offices, all in India, serving 25 states and union territories with exports to over 75 countries contributing 17% of turnover; the Company also operates wind power plants in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

Transformer Oils / Transformer Fluids: mineral, natural ester and synthetic ester-based transformer fluids
Automotive Oils (B2C, retail): lubricants, fluids, greases and coolants compliant with BS VI emission standards

currentContext.strengths: Uniquely positioned as the only global manufacturer offering mineral, natural ester and synthetic ester-based transformer fluids, enabling it to address utility, industrial and infrastructure applications (MD&A, Transformer Fluids)|Among the top two suppliers of White & Mineral Oils in India (Corporate Overview product portfolio)|First Indian lubricant company to manufacture ester molecules; synthetic ester manufacturing capability is being extended to transformer fluids, EV battery cooling and immersion cooling for data centres|Long-standing relationships with leading automotive OEMs, with several partnerships spanning more than two decades|Multi-brand portfolio built over decades - TRANSOL, bioTRANSOL, TRANSOL Synth, TECHNOL, SAVONOL, SAVOGEL, SAVSOL, SAVOFIL, SAVOFLOD, VITAGEL|Export reach across over 75 countries, contributing 17% of total turnover|Debt-free balance sheet and strong cash reserves (Chairman & Managing Director's message)|Captive renewable energy since 1999 - 53.10 MW installed wind capacity and 2061 KWp rooftop solar, with more than 30% of total power consumed at the four manufacturing plants coming from captive solar generation at the respective plant sites

currentContext.expansion: The bundle contains no manufacturing-capacity expansion project, commissioning date or ramp-up plan. Operationally, the Directors' Report records that the Company's Wind Power Plants in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu generated 94.91 MU in FY 2025-2026 against 84.26 MU in the previous year, and that during the year under review the Company did NOT add any new projects to its Wind Portfolio. Renewable and energy-efficiency investment continues at the four existing manufacturing facilities: installed renewable energy capacity of 53.1 MW, rooftop solar of 2,061 kWp installed across the 4 manufacturing facilities, plus energy-efficiency work (expansion of rooftop solar systems, replacement of diesel forklifts with battery-operated electric forklifts, LED lighting, thermic-fluid heating optimisation, insulation upgrades, thermopac overhaul, electric drum heating, energy-efficient pumps, motors and compressors and improved steam distribution), with stated reductions of 9.42% in power consumption at the Turbhe plant, 29.5% in diesel consumption at the Silvassa plant, 1,612 litres of diesel saved at the Kharadpada plant and 8-10% lower LDO consumption at the Mahad plant. Three of the four manufacturing facilities operate as Zero Liquid Discharge units and the fourth is connected to a Common Effluent Treatment Plant. On structure, the Board on 7th May, 2026 approved a Scheme of Amalgamation between Savita GreenTec Limited (Transferor) and Savita Oil Technologies Limited (Transferee) under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals. The BRSR reports that capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were Nil in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25 (R&D on such technologies was 1.04% of total R&D, directed at technologically advanced ester-based products for lubricant, compressor and electric vehicle applications).
currentContext.mdna: Transformer fluids: sustained investment in electricity infrastructure, renewable energy integration and grid modernisation - the global transformer oil market was valued at approximately USD 2.9 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 7.5 billion, growing at a CAGR of over 12% through 2033, with utilities the key demand driver|India transformer demand: expansion of transmission corridors, modernisation of distribution networks and renewable energy evacuation are expected to create sustained demand for transformers and insulating fluids|Customer shift from conventional insulating fluids to advanced fluids offering enhanced fire safety and environmental performance, visible in renewable projects, transportation systems, data centres, industrial facilities and urban utility networks|Ester fluids: the global ester-based transformer oil market was valued at approximately USD 624.83 million in 2025 and is advancing at a 7.73% CAGR from 2026 to 2032; in India, renewable energy, transmission infrastructure, metro rail, airports, data centres and battery energy storage systems (BESS) support adoption|White mineral oils: the global white oil market is expected to reach USD 3,386.3 million by 2033; BS-VI and CAFE norms drive adoption of low-viscosity, synthetic and semi-synthetic lubricants|Electrification: EV registrations increased by around 80% in FY 2025-26 and CNG adoption rose steadily - conventional lubricants still dominate, but the transition creates opportunity for specialised fluids and thermal management solutions|Input costs: fluctuations in crude oil and base oil prices and key raw materials exerted pressure on procurement costs and margins, particularly for imported feedstocks|Domestic capex cycle: Union Budget 2026-27 increased capital expenditure to a record `12.2 lakh crore, up from `11.2 lakh crore, with allocations to roads, railways, ports, airports, power transmission and urban infrastructure|Growth during FY 2025-26 was broad-based - Transformer Oils, White Oils and Exports recorded double-digit growth while the Lubricants business delivered high single-digit growth

risks.risk: Crude oil, base oil and feedstock price volatility
risks.note: The lubricants industry remains exposed to fluctuations in crude oil and base oil prices and competitive pricing pressures; the white mineral oils business is likewise exposed to fluctuations in feedstock costs. As a specialty petroleum manufacturer the Company's procurement cost and margin move with these inputs.

risks.risk: Vehicle electrification and longer lubricant drain intervals
risks.note: Management states that increasing vehicle electrification and lubricant drain intervals may gradually influence lubricant demand across certain segments, even though ICE vehicles still dominate India's automotive base and EV registrations rose around 80% in FY 2025-26.

risks.risk: Long qualification and approval cycles for new fluid technologies
risks.note: Ester-based transformer fluids carry higher costs than conventional mineral oils and face extended qualification cycles and evolving technical standards; for new-age fluids (EV cooling, immersion cooling) commercial adoption remains dependent on technology validation, customer qualification cycles and evolving industry standards - so revenue from the ester pivot is gated by customer approval timelines.

risks.risk: Regulatory and quality-standard tightening in regulated end-uses
risks.note: White mineral oils face evolving regulatory requirements and increasingly stringent quality standards across pharmaceutical, personal care and food-related applications; maintaining consistent product quality and compliance with global standards is stated to be critical for sustained growth.

risks.risk: Competitive intensity, import pressure and ingredient substitution
risks.note: In white mineral oils, competitive intensity, import pressures and shifts towards alternative ingredients in select formulations may influence market dynamics; in lubricants, competitive pricing pressure is explicitly flagged.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and changing regulation for ester fluids
risks.note: Changes in raw material availability and regulatory requirements may influence adoption trends of ester-based transformer fluids across certain applications.

risks.risk: Emission and efficiency regulation reshaping product requirements
risks.note: BS-VI emission standards and CAFE norms continue to reshape lubricant requirements, driving a shift to low-viscosity, synthetic and semi-synthetic grades - a reformulation and requalification burden as well as a premiumisation opportunity.

risks.risk: Process, fire and occupational safety at manufacturing plants
risks.note: Handling of petroleum products requires an ISO 45001:2018-based OH&S management system, HIRA, permit-to-work, LOTO and extensive fire infrastructure (hydrant systems on dedicated 100 KL, 225 KL and 650 KL water storage tanks at 7 kg/cm2). Zero LTIFR, zero recordable injuries and zero fatalities were reported for employees and workers in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.

themes.title: Transformer & grid-component shortage
themes.need: Transformer makers are running flat-out at record order books even as core-capacity ramps land (ATLANTAELE 16k->63k MVA, Q1FY27 record order book INR3,117cr on record INR972cr quarterly inflow, Vadod now PGCIL 400kV-approved with a 765kV tech tie-up in final talks; TARIL toward 75k+ MVA, Q1FY27 UEOB INR6,630cr +26% YoY on a >INR1,000cr single-shot PGCIL Ultra-Mega order, though a Changodar-expansion air-pocket held Q1 revenue to +10%; SHILCTECH adding 220kV) yet the binding constraint is still everything INSIDE a transformer - CRGO core steel, CTC/winding wire (KSHINTL/BHAGYANGR), bushings/insulators (YASHHV; 18-24mo lead, ~95% RIP/OIP imported) and transformer oil (APARINDS); both OEMs are now backward-integrating to own the bottleneck (TARIL's INR900-1,000cr CRGO/CTC/bushing/pressboard programme). Capacity-gated supply is the repeated 'need of the hour' and is driving pricing power now, though both OEMs flagged ~60,000 MVA of new 400kV capacity landing industry-wide in 3-4 months as a 1-year-out overcapacity watch-item (neither sees pricing pressure yet).
themes.driver: PGCIL Ultra-Mega order conversion (TARIL's first >INR1,000cr single-shot award) + Vadod/Changodar capacity ramps; 400kV short-circuit tests and 765kV PGCIL approvals due by Q2FY27-end are the next re-rating triggers; TARIL's Changodar restart (Aug-2026) is the swing quarter for its own growth reacceleration.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.
